Seminar Title:

Artificial Intelligence and Data-Driven Optimization in Steelmaking

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Metallurgical and Materials Engineering

Speaker Name:

Manish Kumar Singh ( Rollno : 518mm9011)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

MM202 (Metallurgical and Materials Engg. Annex Building)

Date and Time:

16 Sep 2026 03:00 PM

Contact:

Snehanshu Pal

Abstract:

Steelmaking has traditionally been analysed using first-principles models such as thermodynamics and mass-energy balances. With the advancement of Industry 4.0, the availability of process data has enabled the adoption of machine learning (ML) for prediction, optimisation, and decision support. In this work, an evolutionary neural network (EvoNN)-based multi-objective optimisation is applied to basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steelmaking to achieve low phosphorus with conflicting objectives: (i) minimising phosphorus while maximising turndown temperature, and (ii) minimising phosphorus along with FeO content in slag. Pareto front analysis identifies optimal limits for temperature and FeO, providing operational guidelines to improve dephosphorization. A reliable machine learning (RML) framework based on stacking regression is developed for temperature prediction across BOF, ladle furnace (LF), RH degasser, and continuous casting (CCM). The two-layer stacking model, comprising eight ML algorithms with feature selection using variance inflation factor, achieves prediction accuracy of 95&ndash99%. Furthermore, a multilayer stacked regression model comprising four ML algorithms is utilised to predict the viscosity of BOF slag. A systematic framework is used to select optimal meta-models and evaluate multiple stacking configurations, achieving an accuracy of 0.993 with minimal training time. This study emphasizes the efficacy of optimal-configured stacking regression models in industrial applications, achieving both maximum accuracy and minimal computational time.
